claims.summary: For N >= N_0 and a rectangle Q=[0,a]x[0,b] with 1 <= a/b <= (log N)^(1/2) there is a fixed N-point set Z in Q, whose cells tile Q with area ab/N and diameter at most K sqrt(ab/N), such that for X_1..X_N i.i.d. uniform on Q, with probability at least 1-2(log N)^(1/2) N^(-2)-L (log N)^(1/2) exp(-(log N)^(3/2)/(3L)), some matching moves each coordinate by at most K sqrt(ab/N)(log N)^(3/4), K and L universal.
claims.assessment: Working proof: quantile strips equalize the strip counts at horizontal cost a sqrt(log N/N) (Hoeffding at the M-1 inner quantiles), which fits the Leighton-Shor scale exactly up to aspect (log N)^(1/2); in each strip the monograph's Theorem 4.7.1, whose deterministic part (Appendix B.3) uses the points only through the discrepancy events (4.103) and (B.10) on a coarser grid, tolerates the one boundary point once it is moved off the grid. The aspect bound is this method's limit, not a proved threshold.
claims.rationale: Extends the Leighton-Shor upper bound to the elongated rectangles that the exponent pairs of the ultimate matching curve produce after rescaling.

claims.summary: For alpha_1,alpha_2 in (0,infinity], u_j=(log N)^(1/alpha_j), X i.i.d. uniform on [0,1]^2 and Y evenly spread or an independent uniform sample: if 1/alpha_1+1/alpha_2 >= 1/2, with probability tending to one some matching has max_i |X_i^j-Y^j_pi(i)| <= K u_j sqrt(log N/N) for j=1,2, K universal; if 1/alpha_1+1/alpha_2 < 1/2, for every K this fails with probability tending to one. So the maximum-displacement consequence of the ultimate matching conjecture holds exactly on and above its curve.
claims.assessment: Working proof: capping 1/alpha_j at 1/2, rescaling each coordinate by u_j and lem:anisotropic-leighton-shor-bound for (i), with a Hall argument to the evenly spread Y or composition through the common set for two samples; (ii) is the proof of thm:below-curve-matching-exclusion, which uses only maximal displacements.
claims.rationale: Proves the conjecture's maximum consequence at every pair of the curve and shows that a refutation on the curve must use the joint exponential moments, not maximal displacements.
claims.next_action: Control the intermediate levels: the number of pairs with displacement above s t^(1/alpha_j) for 1 << t << log N.
